The claim that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus, leading to an increase in COVID-19 cases where 5G was installed, is false. There is no scientific evidence to support a link between 5G technology and the spread of COVID-19. [1] [2] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7] [8] [9]

COVID-19 is a viral disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus, and it spreads through respiratory droplets when an infected person coughs, sneezes, or speaks. [3] [4] Viruses cannot travel on radio waves or mobile networks. [3]

Conspiracy theories linking 5G to the coronavirus pandemic have circulated online, leading to incidents such as the burning of cell towers in the UK and other European countries. [1] [2] [6] [7] These theories often suggest that 5G either causes the virus, weakens the immune system, or that Wuhan, the origin of the virus, was the first city to roll out 5G. [2] [5] [8] [9] However, regulators have set limits on the radiation power of 5G devices, and 5G uses non-ionizing radiation, which does not damage DNA or cause cancer. [1] [4] [5] [8] Furthermore, COVID-19 has spread in many countries that do not have 5G networks. [3] Organizations like the UN's International Telecommunications Union (ITU) and the World Health Organization (WHO) have stated that there is no connection between 5G and COVID-19. [7] [8]
